tip: 'Era preciso que' (it was necessary that) forces the subjunctive: 'que todos colaborassem', not 'colaboraram'.
'Têm' with the circumflex is the plural "have" ('eles têm'); the singular 'tem' has no accent.
The preposition 'a' and the article 'o' contract into 'ao': 'tenho ido ao dentista', never 'a o dentista'.
Portuguese builds the compound past with 'ter', not 'haver': 'tínhamos ouvido' = "we had heard".
'Como se' (as if) takes the past subjunctive: 'como se nada tivesse acontecido', not 'tinha acontecido'.
'Mudar-se' with the pronoun means to move house, not just to change: 'tinha se mudado para o bairro'.
'Desejar que' triggers the subjunctive for a wish: 'desejava que meus filhos tivessem mais oportunidades'.
'A fim de que' (so that) states purpose and takes the subjunctive: 'a fim de que todos entendam'.
'Fazer academia' is the everyday phrase for working out at the gym: 'tem feito academia todo dia'.
'Mesmo que' (even if) always takes the subjunctive: 'mesmo que ele quisesse', not 'mesmo que queria'.
Unreal conditions pair 'se' plus the '-sse' subjunctive ('pagasse') with a conditional result ('sairia').
'Escrever' has the irregular participle 'escrito', not 'escrevido': 'tinha escrito o relatório'.
'Dar certo' is a fixed phrase meaning to work out or turn out well: 'não ia dar certo'.
'Ganhar' has two participles; with 'ter' the regular 'ganhado' is the traditional choice: 'tinha ganhado o prêmio'.
'Pôr' has the irregular participle 'posto': 'tinha posto a mesa' = had set the table.
'Agradecer' takes 'a' before the person thanked: 'agradecer a todos', not 'agradecer todos'.
'Tinha acabado de' + infinitive = "had just" done something.
'Quem dera' expresses a wish and takes the past subjunctive: 'quem dera a gente morasse perto'.
'Haver' meaning there is or there are becomes 'houvesse' in the past subjunctive: 'se houvesse mais vagas'.
'Se eu soubesse' can mean both "if I knew" and "if I had known"; the same '-sse' form often covers present and past hypotheticals.
'Entregues' agrees in gender and number with the subject 'documentos'.
'Viu' at the end works like "right?" or "okay?", a spoken tag checking the listener got it, not a literal "you saw".
Hypotheticals pair 'se' plus the '-sse' subjunctive ('pudéssemos') with the '-ria' conditional ('ficaríamos') in the result.
After the impersonal 'é recomendável', use a plain infinitive ('beber'); a conjugated verb would need 'que' first.
'Como se', meaning as if, always takes the subjunctive; 'tivesse parado' is the past form for something that had happened.
Verbs of requesting like 'pedir que' push the following verb into the subjunctive: 'trouxesse', not 'trouxe'.
'Costuma' plus an infinitive ('almoçar') means usually does something; it stands in for the English adverb "usually".
'Se eu fosse você' is the set phrase for giving advice, "if I were you"; 'fosse' is the subjunctive of 'ser'.
'Houvesse' is the "there were" form of 'haver'; like 'há', it stays singular no matter how many things follow ('opções').
Future passive: 'será'/'serão' plus a participle; the participle agrees with the subject, so feminine 'exposição' takes 'aberta'.
